output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter than Quillan. Dryer D5 has degraded, with dew point around −16 to −19 °C against −40 °C, and its alarm limit was loosened in week 31. Together they leave resin at the Press 5 throat at 0.25–0.31% moisture against a 0.20% limit. That gives splay and latch cracks. Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10%. Press 5 with Quillan rejects 0.9%. Press 7, which has a good dryer, rejects about 0.8% with either supplier. Arnholt dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 rejected 0.8%. The second-shift gap exists because Press 5 is the only press that runs VX on second shift. New and experienced operators reject at the same rate on each resin, so do not discipline the new operators. Dropping Arnholt is not warranted. The trial missed this because it ran on Press 7 only. I'm quite sure of this. The one open point is whether storing Arnholt in the north annex explains its wetter inlet resin. Annex storage and supplier are confounded in the samples. Next steps: repair D5 and its heater, change the desiccant, and restore the −40 alarm limit. Keep Arnholt off D5 until the dew point is verified. Add a throat moisture check for every lot. Test annex storage separately before paying to move stock.
